345739.review_depth: source v1-v3 introduction read (Conjecture 1.1 of arXiv:2003.02679, attributed to De Loera, Haws and Koeppe); published refutation identified
345739.disposition: The positivity half of the conjunction was refuted by L. Ferroni, 'Matroids are not Ehrhart positive', Adv. Math. 402 (2022) 108337, arXiv:2105.04465. Ferroni gives sparse paving matroids whose Ehrhart polynomial has a negative coefficient. That makes the literal conjunction false; it is a known published result, so zero credit. The h*-unimodality half stays open, but it is a different statement.
prior_art: arXiv:2105.04465v3 (Ferroni). The PDF is cached as sources/ferroni.pdf (sha256 e2a06c6c9ac5d60a0b89e0e08ba7f12b0d103321f8078f29f040e71ece39894f). The abstract, read in sources2/ferroni.txt, says the paper disproves the De Loera-Haws-Koeppe positivity conjecture: for every n >= 19 there are connected matroids that are not Ehrhart positive.

345810.review_depth: source v1 and v2 read around Conjecture 23 (arXiv:2003.04804v2, line 797); bounded literature search
345810.disposition: The source is Dailly, Hansberg and Ventura. 'Balanceable' there is the Caro-Hansberg-Montejano Ramsey-type notion for 2-colourings of K_n. The MathDB paraphrase instead defines it via signings in which every cycle has equally many positive and negative edges, which is a paraphrase defect. The claim is NP-completeness of recognising balanceability. Milanic and Servatius (arXiv:2403.05418) prove NP-completeness only for simple balanceability of 9-regular graphs; the general problem remains open. A complexity-theoretic NP-hardness proof is not a finite or Lean-feasible target in this lane, so it is parked.

345842.review_depth: source (Mynhardt-Nasserasr survey, arXiv:2003.05956v1) read around Conjecture 3.1
345842.disposition: The conjecture is Bonsma-Cereceda's: diam C_k(G) = O(n^3) for k >= col(G)+1. It is a well-known open reconfiguration conjecture, closely tied to Cereceda's conjecture. Known partial results include Bousquet-Heinrich's O(n^{d+1}) bound. No finite mechanism is available, so it is parked.

345985.review_depth: source v1 and v2 checked; published proof identified via search (abstract and bibliographic data)
345985.disposition: The conjecture was proved by Garbe, Kral', Malekshahian and Penaguiao, 'The dimension of the feasible region of pattern densities', arXiv:2309.10203; Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 178 (2025) 1-14. They show the dimension equals the number of non-trivial Lyndon permutations of size at most k. The theorem body was not read in this lane; the abstract states the full scope.

346016.review_depth: source v1-v4 read around Conjectures 6.10-6.12 and Table 1 (arXiv:2003.13777v4, lines 1607-1630)
346016.disposition: The authors verified the conjecture for S0, S1, S2, N1, N2, N3 and N4 using complete lists of irreducible triangulations. Going beyond that needs irreducible-triangulation lists for further surfaces, which are not available here. Small-n cases where K_n embeds are trivial. No counterexample mechanism was found, so it is parked.

346042.review_depth: source v1 and v2 read (Definition 7.6, Conjecture 7.7); resolving corollary body read
346042.disposition: The conjecture is resolved by Berget, Eur, Spink and Tseng, 'Tautological classes of matroids', arXiv:2103.08021, Corollary 11.5 ('We also resolve [DES21, Conjecture 7.7]'). For loopless M of rank r they prove KT_{U_{1,E},M}(x,0) = x^r, hence Kchi(q) = (-1)^r KT(1-q,0) = (q-1)^r. Published (Invent. Math. 2023); zero credit.

346303.review_depth: source v1-v3 read (Conjecture 5.2 in v3 = Conjecture 7.2 in v1/v2); Monte Carlo diagnostic
346303.disposition: Literally the claim is E[Delta_1(t,x)] ~ ||x - xbar||_2 for every t = o(n log n). It already fails at t = 0, since Delta_1(0,x) = ||x||_1 = 2n/(n+1) -> 2 while ||x - xbar||_2 = sqrt(n/(n+1)) -> 1. A Monte Carlo run on S_2000 gives E Delta_1 approximately 1.999, 1.947 and 1.878 at t = 0, n/2 and n. For fixed t/n = c the value tends to a c-dependent limit, so no '~ constant' statement can hold. This is a wording/endpoint defect of the printed statement; refuting it earns zero credit. The intended Theta(1)-until-n log n statement is not determinable from the source.

346342.review_depth: source v1 read (Conjecture 4.12, Lemma 4.13); follow-up arXiv:2007.01412v2 grepped (Example 6.3)
346342.disposition: Conjecture 4.12 asks for an exhaustive rigid 2-partition with mu_2(G) <= min mu_2(G_i). The source proves it for graphs with a bridge, hence for all trees. The follow-up by Hofmann, Kennedy, Mugnolo and Pluemer (Example 6.3) shows that a different monotonicity fails, but not this conjecture. A counterexample needs exact metric-graph eigenvalue computations; this is not Lean-feasible, so it is parked.

346431.review_depth: source v1 read around Conjecture 2 (arXiv:2005.04252v1, lines 120-150)
346431.disposition: Conjecture 2 (pinned broken-line shelling) strengthens Stanley's pure O-sequence conjecture for matroid h-vectors, which is a famous open problem. A small-matroid counterexample search would need a faithful implementation of broken-line shellings of dual matroid polytopes; that was not attempted for lack of time. Parked.

346465.review_depth: source v1 read (two-birds family and Conjecture 14, lines 395-426); divisibility and occurrence computations; bounded literature search
346465.disposition: A proof for every k needs a uniform binary construction. Bounded computation shows that T_k is not divisible by T_j for 3 <= j < k <= 7, as expected for minimally avoidable formulas, so lambda(T_3) = 2 does not transfer. The Thue-Morse word contains occurrences of T_3 through T_6 with image lengths <= 8. No published resolution was found. Parked.

In v2 and v3 the authors construct nonisomorphic triangle-free graphs, of arbitrarily high girth, with equal chromatic symmetric function from Brylawski's graph via their Theorem 11. v3 says this 'is particularly noteworthy since there has not previously been shown even triangle-free graphs with the same chromatic symmetric function'. 346238.review_depth: source v1 and v2 read: Algorithms 1 and 3, Lemmas 1-7, Section 6 (Proposition 2), Examples 3 and 7, Conjecture 1. The implementation was validated against both worked examples.
346238.disposition: scripts/gjpo.py implements GPO/GJPO faithfully. Validation: it reproduces Example 7 (n = m+1 = 5, outside the conjecture's range: 128 pairs, 96 inequivalent sequences, multiplicity histogram 70/23/1/1/1) and all eight printed sequences of Example 3. Exhaustive search over every nonsingular h, every rooted spanning tree of the PAG and every initial state in the root cycle covers: m=1, n=3..7; m=2, n=4..8; m=3, n=5..8; m=4, n=6..8; and m=5, n=7 (65536 functions h, 9295360 rooted trees, 59070464 input pairs). It found no collision, and every run produced a de Bruijn sequence. Collisions reduce to a combinatorial condition on cycle intervals that split few conjugate pairs (candidates/346238/NOTES.md), but no proof was obtained. This is a bounded non-finding, so the item is parked.

346320.disposition: Conjecture 6.2 fails for SRK = S1S2. Take y = (1/2,1,1,1,1,1) and x_{04} = x_{05} = x_{23} = x_{25} = x_{34} = 1/2, x_{12} = x_{13} = x_{45} = 1, all other x = 0; this point lies in P_A^{K_6}. Run A (S1 on {4,5}, S1 on {1,2}, S2 on {12,3}) ends with 3 vertices. Run B (S1 on {1,2}, S2 on {12,3}; then {4,5} has no S1 witness) ends with 4 vertices. Both runs are executions of Algorithm S1S2, verified literally in exact arithmetic by scripts/verify_346320.py. The final graphs have different orders, so they are not isomorphic. Search coverage: exhaustive half-integral search for n <= 7, covering all classes at n = 7 including the all-value-1 class (52065 labelled inputs), finds failures only for S1S2. Random samples with denominators 2-4 on 7-10 vertices also fail only for S1S2. Caveats: the later paper by the same group drops S2 for practical reasons, and a reviewer may judge the non-confluence mechanism routine. Ordinary proof: candidates/346320/PROOF.md.
